subject: microbiology
title: Innate and Acquired Immunity, Active and Passive Immunity and Adjuvants

steps.tx: **Innate immunity** is preformed and immediate: skin and mucosal barriers, gastric acid and lysozyme, complement alternative pathway, phagocytes, NK cells and pattern recognition receptors reading microbial signatures (PAMPs) through Toll like receptors. It has no memory and no specificity beyond patterns, yet decides most microbial encounters before adaptive immunity wakes, and its defects present as defined infectious phenotypes.
steps.say: Born ready, pattern specific, memory free: innate immunity fights tonight's invasion.

right.title: Innate character
points: Instructs adaptive response via dendritic cells

steps.tx: **Innate immunity** is already formed and acts at once. Skin and mucosa bar entry. Gastric acid and lysozyme damage microbes that get further. The alternative complement pathway, phagocytes, and natural killer cells respond without a prior lesson. Pattern recognition receptors, including Toll like receptors, read microbial signatures called pathogen associated molecular patterns. There is no memory, and specificity stops at those patterns. Most encounters are settled before adaptive immunity is awake. When a piece of this system is missing, the infections that follow form a recognisable pattern.
steps.say: Innate immunity is immediate and has no memory. Barriers, acid, lysozyme, alternative pathway complement, phagocytes, and natural killer cells act before lymphocytes learn the invader. Toll like receptors read microbial patterns rather than one exact antigen. Most microbes are stopped here. Missing pieces produce characteristic infection patterns.

vis.alt: A timeline compares immediate innate defences with the slower start and later memory of adaptive immunity.
vis.caption: Barriers, complement, phagocytes, and pattern receptors act at once, while adaptive responses rise later and leave memory. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Acquired (adaptive) immunity** answers with specific receptors built by gene rearrangement: B cell antibodies (humoral) and T cell receptors (cellular), clonal expansion over days, and memory that accelerates and strengthens re encounters. Primary responses lag and lead with IgM; secondary responses are faster, higher and IgG dominated, the kinetics every vaccine schedule exploits.
steps.say: Adaptive immunity is slow first and swift forever after; memory is its signature.

right.title: Secondary response
points: Lag short, titre high and sustained
Memory B and T cells persist years

steps.tx: **Active immunity** is self made after infection or vaccination (slow, durable, memory bearing), while **passive immunity** is borrowed antibody: maternal IgG across placenta and IgA in milk, immunoglobulin preparations, monoclonal antibodies and antitoxins, immediate but months brief and memory free. Comparing their onset and duration answers a permanent examination duo.
steps.say: Active is earned slowly and kept; passive arrives tonight and leaves by season's end.

left.title: Active immunity
points: Onset weeks, duration years to life

right.title: Passive immunity
points: Maternal IgG and breast milk IgA
No memory; repeat for continued cover

steps.tx: **Adjuvants** are vaccine ingredients that wake innate immunity so adaptive responses amplify: alum (depot and inflammasome traditions), oil emulsions, TLR agonists (MPL, CpG), and saponin systems in modern subunit vaccines, without which purified antigens often tolerise or whisper. Adjuvant selection explains why subunit vaccines protect at all and why reactogenicity profiles differ by product.
steps.say: Pure antigen whispers; adjuvant knocks on the innate door so the lesson is heard.

left.title: Adjuvant roster
points: MF59 and AS03 oil emulsions: influenza
AS04 (MPL plus alum): HPV and hepatitis B
AS01 (saponin plus MPL): shingles and malaria

right.title: Adjuvant effects
points: Broader and longer responses in elderly

steps.tx: **Herd immunity** emerges when immune proportion interrupts transmission chains, protecting the unvaccinable (newborns, chemotherapy patients) at thresholds set by R0 and vaccine effectiveness (measles demanding mid ninety percents). It is a community pharmacokinetics of immunity, eroded by clustering of refusal even where average coverage looks adequate.
steps.say: Averages hide pockets; measles finds the unimmune cluster, not the national mean.

steps.tx: **Pattern recognition** deserves its mechanisms: TLR4 reads LPS, TLR2 peptidoglycan and lipoteichoic acid, TLR5 flagellin, TLR3, 7, 8 and 9 read nucleic acids in endosomes, NLRs and RIG like receptors patrol cytosol, and mannose receptors and scavenger pathways assist phagocytosis. Their signalling (MyD88, NF kappa B) writes cytokine weather the cytokine lesson spends.
steps.say: Each microbial signature has a named reader; the readers write the cytokine weather.

steps.tx: **Phagocyte killing machinery** bridges to immunodeficiency: ingestion, phagolysosome fusion, oxidative burst (NADPH oxidase superoxide), nitric oxide and granule enzymes, with opsonins (IgG Fc, C3b) multiplying grip. Chronic granulomatous disease knocks out the burst; leukocyte adhesion deficiency stops arrival; each defect's organism roster (catalase positive bacteria and fungi) is mechanism read clinically.
steps.say: Arrive, grip, engulf, burn: each verb is a named immunodeficiency when missing.

right.title: Defect phenotypes
points: LAD: no pus, delayed cord separation
Chediak Higashi: giant granules, silvery hair
Neutropenia: mucosal and skin sepsis tempo

steps.tx: **Phagocyte killing** runs through arrival, grip, ingestion, and burning. Opsonins such as IgG Fc and C3b multiply the grip. The phagosome then fuses with lysosomes. NADPH oxidase makes superoxide in the oxidative burst, and nitric oxide plus granule enzymes add further killing. Chronic granulomatous disease removes the burst, so catalase positive bacteria and fungi survive inside the cell. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency stops the phagocyte arriving at all. Each missing verb produces its own list of organisms, which is how the defect is read at the bedside.
steps.say: Neutrophils must arrive, grip with help from IgG and C3b, engulf, and then kill. NADPH oxidase supplies the oxidative burst of superoxide, with nitric oxide and granules beside it. Chronic granulomatous disease keeps the burst off, so catalase positive bacteria and fungi persist. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency blocks arrival itself.

vis.alt: A sequence shows a neutrophil ingesting a microbe, fusing the phagosome with granules, and generating an oxidative burst.
vis.caption: Opsonised prey is gripped, engulfed, and exposed to superoxide from NADPH oxidase plus granule enzymes inside the phagolysosome. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Acute phase response** systemises innate output: IL 1, IL 6 and TNF from macrophages instruct hepatic CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin and serum amyloid A, fever via hypothalamic prostaglandins, and marrow neutrophilia, giving clinicians CRP and procalcitonin as its gauges. These mediators become sepsis physiology when the pattern response loses its local address.
steps.say: CRP is the liver reporting macrophage cytokine weather; sepsis is that weather gone national.

right.title: Clinical gauges
points: CRP kinetics over days, not minutes
